title: Extension of reductive equivariant torsors across the nodal origin
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $\pi$ a uniformizer and $k=A/(\pi)$ its residue field. An $A$-group scheme means a group object in schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}A$: the multiplication, unit and inverse diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with this base in place of the field base. Write $\mathbf G_{m,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finite-type $A$-group scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $H$ is reductive, meaning every geometric fibre is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Here unipotent means that every geometric point is a unipotent matrix in a faithful representation. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A[s,t]/(st-\pi)$, with $\mathbf G_{m,A}$ acting by $z\cdot(s,t)=(zs,z^{-1}t)$, and let $o=V(s,t)=\operatorname{Spec}k$. A right $H$-torsor over an $A$-scheme $Y$ means a represented right torsor in [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors], with base $\operatorname{Spec}A$. A $\mathbf G_m$-equivariant such torsor has a left $\mathbf G_{m,A}$-action covering the specified action on $Y$ and commuting with the right $H$-action; isomorphisms respect both actions and the projection to $Y$. Write $U=X\setminus\{o\}=D(s)\cup D(t)$. For every $\mathbf G_{m,A}$-equivariant right $H$-torsor $P\to U$, there are a $\mathbf G_{m,A}$-equivariant right $H$-torsor $\widetilde P\to X$ and an equivariant torsor isomorphism $\widetilde P|_U\simeq P$. No completeness, splitness or residue-field perfection assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Choose $i:H\hookrightarrow L=\operatorname{GL}_{n,A}$ and the affine quotient $L/H$ by [lem-sfb-dvr-reductive-linear-affine-quotient]. Apply [lem-sfb-linear-torsor-reduction-sections] to $P$ on $U$: obtain $E=P\times^H L$, its rank-$n$ bundle $V$, and a section $\sigma:U\to E/H$. Naturality gives the $\mathbf G_m$-linearization of $V$ and equivariance of $\sigma$ from the given commuting actions.

source.place: Section 2, Claim 2, first two sentences; general DVR embedding supplied by Milne VIII Aside 9.4 and quotient affineness by Alper Corollary 9.7.7.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-nodal-surface-flat-hartogs], $X$ is an integral regular Noetherian surface and $o$ has codimension two. Hence [lem-sfb-regular-surface-vector-bundle-extension] gives $\widetilde V=j_*V$, finite locally free of rank $n$. On $T=\mathbf G_m\times_A X$, projection to $X$ is flat. The action map is projection composed with $(z,x)\mapsto(z,zx)$, an automorphism with inverse $(z,x)\mapsto(z,z^{-1}x)$. The two pullbacks of $\widetilde V$ are bundles; their isomorphism over $\mathbf G_m\times_A U$ and its inverse extend uniquely by the Hom clause of [lem-sfb-nodal-surface-flat-hartogs]. Their composites are identities by the same injectivity. The identity and cocycle laws hold because they hold on $U$ and Hom restriction is injective on $X$ and $\mathbf G_m^2\times_A X$. Thus $\widetilde V$ is linearized, and [lem-sfb-linear-torsor-reduction-sections] gives its equivariant frame torsor $\widetilde E$, extending $E$.

source.place: Section 2, Claim 2, vector-bundle extension, with the equivariance argument made explicit by flat-base Hartogs.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-linear-torsor-reduction-sections], $Z=\widetilde E/H$ is affine over $X$. The section $\sigma$ extends uniquely to $\widetilde\sigma:X\to Z$ by the affine-section clause of [lem-sfb-nodal-surface-flat-hartogs] for $T=X$. On $\mathbf G_m\times_A X$ the two sections expressing its equivariance agree over $\mathbf G_m\times_A U$, so the same clause, for this flat projection, makes them equal everywhere. Thus $\widetilde\sigma$ is equivariant.

source.place: Section 2, Claim 2, last two sentences; uniqueness also over the action parameter.

proof.text: Set $\widetilde P=\widetilde E\times_{Z,\widetilde\sigma}X$. The inverse construction of [lem-sfb-linear-torsor-reduction-sections] makes it a represented right $H$-torsor. The invariant section makes this fibre product stable under the left $\mathbf G_m$-action on $\widetilde E$, which commutes with the right $H$-action. Over $U$ the construction recovers $(E,\sigma)$ and hence $P$, with both actions respected, by the same equivalence. This proves the required extension for arbitrary $A$ and $k$.

source.place: Section 2, Claim 2, reduction recovered from the extended section.

Source check: Alper–Halpern-Leistner–Heinloth (author-hosted PDF), Section 2 Claim 2, p.2. Its proof is: embed G in GL_n; a G-torsor is the same as a GL_n-torsor plus a section of E/G; j_*V is the unique vector-bundle extension because X is regular and the origin has codimension 2; Ẽ/G is affine because G is reductive; the section extends because Γ(X,O)=Γ(X∖0,O). Neither completeness nor algebraic closure of the residue field is used there (they enter in Claim 3), so the item's generality is supported. The four steps realise this proof faithfully. Equivariance is done explicitly: the action isomorphism and its inverse extend on G_m×X along flat maps, the unit law is checked on X and the cocycle law on G_m²×X, and the extended section is equivariant by uniqueness on G_m×X. Stacks 0EBJ (lemma-reflexive-S2-extend) plus 0B3N (lemma-reflexive-over-regular-dim-2) give exactly lem-sfb-regular-surface-vector-bundle-extension. lem-sfb-nodal-surface-flat-hartogs is true: B is a regular domain of dimension 2, B = B_s ∩ B_t inside B_st, and the equalizer stays exact after flat base change, which gives the Hom and affine-section clauses with no Noetherian hypothesis on T. lem-sfb-dvr-reductive-linear-affine-quotient is true: a closed linear embedding over a DVR via a finite free subcomodule, and GL_n/H affine by Alper Cor. 9.7.7. Small cases checked: H=1, G_m, GL_n; A=Z_(p); T empty. No duplicates found: the nearest existing nodes are lem-sbc-affine-depth-two-locally-free-model (only a coherent model), lem-sfb-normal-extension-torsor-reduction (normal subgroup, over a field), Q25's lem-sfb-nodal-equivariant-torsor-rigidity and the field-only group lemmas. No new node restates the item; the nodes cite only definitions, so there is no cycle; no SGA is cited. FIX (B2/E5): the last sentence of lem-sfb-linear-torsor-reduction-sections relied on undefined notions ('linearized bundle', 'invariant section') that item steps 1, 2 and 4 use. It is replaced by a precise dictionary: a G-action on a torsor covering a and commuting with the right action is a torsor isomorphism pr^*P≅a^*P with unit and cocycle laws; under the frame equivalence this is a G-linearization pr^*V≅a^*V; under the reduction equivalence it is an equivariant E with a section σ such that φ sends pr^*σ to a^*σ. Only the statement changed; the whole node is in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/. Advisory, not changed: the item's word 'affine' has no citation (inherited from Q25).
